race_name: Fred Whitton Challenge — The Daddy of Them All

top_categories.workout_context: 114ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Fred Whitton Challenge — The Daddy of Them All's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.

Road-specific control matters at Fred Whitton Challenge — The Daddy of Them All. Practice on paved Lake District mountain passes with extreme: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 112 miles.
At Fred Whitton Challenge — The Daddy of Them All, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 112, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
12,795ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Fred Whitton Challenge — The Daddy of Them All. Train it until it feels boring.
12,795ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Fred Whitton Challenge — The Daddy of Them All. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 12,795ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 12,795ft of climbing on paved Lake District mountain passes with extreme does to your power file on race day.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved Lake District mountain passes with extreme can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Fred Whitton Challenge — The Daddy of Them All’s 112 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Fred Whitton Challenge — The Daddy of Them All rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on paved lake district mountain passes with extreme gradients to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Road Specific to prepare you for 112 miles of paved lake district mountain passes with extreme gradients in Grasmere, Lake District, Cumbria, England, UK.
